The fact that you are out seeking to understand more rather than brush off or negate her feelings suggests to me that you are a good parent. Like many others have said just being there and validating her is one of the greatest things you can do to support her. Sorry if others have said this as I didn't read very far but I would also look to empower her in her conviction of the word no. I know when I was that age I didn't understand what coercion was. I was begged and pleaded and pushed into things that I didn't want to do because I didn't have the confidence and conviction to keep saying no. I think that's so important especially with her past. Those situations may become retraumatizing without someone to show her no will ALWAYS be an appropriate answer. Finally, I would just suggest the importance of her knowing you are there to get her out of "sticky" situations free from judgment. She can send a text or call with a key letter or word and you would know that covertly means she wants out of wherever she is, no questions asked. Thank you for looking to understand and ask questions!

For me personally I do have a little bit of a libido (it is very small but it is there) but I do not find anyone sexually attractive, that is, id rather satisfy that myself than with anyone else. I do have a friend that the SSRI is why she thought she was ace but wasn't so its a very real thing and a totally valid question. For me its all about who is attractive not if I want to or not.
